newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end up slightly, Coltabaco soars.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end up slightly, Coltabaco soars.

text.p: Colombian stocks edged up slightly in lackluster trade, with only cigarette maker Coltabaco and Banco de Colombia shining in today's action, traders said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index nudged 0.08 percent higher to 18,752.16 points amid volume of 2.54 billion pesos. Meanwhile, Bogota's IBB was up the same 0.08 percent to 1,232.64 in trade of 4.3 billion pesos.
Coltabaco jumped 8.10 percent to 4,000 on 193 million shares traded in Bogota, and finished the day in Medellin at the same price on volume of 141 million.

Coltabaco's jump was attributed to a shortage of its stock in the market, and as part of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno, it is much favored by local investors. Also, other units of the Antioqueno holding company have recently reported solid results.
Banco de Colombia, the country's second largest bank in assets, rose 1.5 percent to 416 in Bogota, and by 0.97 percent in Medellin to the same price.
Banco de Colombia is perceived as being undervalued, and local investors see it as a good stock to speculate on, traders said.
"Among the shares on offer, Banco de Colombia is the cheapest, one of the easiest to come by, and one of the best ones to speculate on," a Bogota broker said.
Banco de Bogota, headed by finance magnate Luis Carlos Sarmiento, slipped 0.28 percent to 7,120 on the Bogota exchange. The stock ended the day at 7,100 in Medellin.
